h.select_rule: Keep hypotheses you rate at least 55% likely true but expect other models to rate below 50%, and name the specific naive reasoning that would mislead them. Drop anything you rate below 50% yourself, and anything obvious from structure alone. Keep fields and directions diverse.
h.strategy: Propose a broad, varied set of conditional hypotheses covering many different edited fields, conditioning fields and both directions. For each, briefly note your own probability that it holds and how an intuitive reader would judge it.

hyps.why: Removing a parameter-free pooling edge costs little compared with removing a conv or skip, and can even help.
Removing a conv edge hurts more than removing a parameter-free edge.
Parallel conv inputs to the output show diminishing returns.
A strong direct conv edge reduces the marginal value of another conv into node 3.
With a strong conv already feeding the output, an extra conv adds less.
With edge 4 cut, edge 0 reaches the output only through the longer path via edge 2 and edge 5.
Node 2 then has less incoming signal, so a conv on edge 5 is less useful.
Pooling replacing none restores a connection, whereas replacing other ops does not.
Cutting a strong conv on the sole exit of node 2 is very harmful.
Upgrading 1x1 to 3x3 gives only a small gain compared with filling an empty or weak edge.
